concerns.concern: The fitted relaxation times (24,000 to 160,000 s) are 5 to 50 times longer than the measurement windows, and the g₂ contrast is tiny. τ and β are therefore strongly covariant and poorly constrained, and the quoted uncertainties are implausibly small.
concerns.quote: These are 5–50× longer than the windows (~3,000–10,000 s) over which each g₂ is measured.

concerns.concern: The stated instrumental stability limit (8000 ± 3000 s) is below most reported τ values (e.g., 81,000 s at 298 K). The current-driven slow dynamics may therefore be indistinguishable from instrumental drift.
concerns.quote: If the latter, the current-driven "slow dynamics" are indistinguishable from instrumental drift.

concerns.concern: One τ is fitted for all aging times while β varies. A slowing τ could then be absorbed into a rising β, making the β ≈ 1 → 1.5 'transition' a fitting artifact.
concerns.quote: The β ≈ 1 → 1.5 "transition" may thus be a parametrization artifact.

concerns.concern: A compressed exponent (β > 1) is not diagnostic of jamming. Joule-heating-induced thermal drift, Bragg-peak walking, heterodyne mixing or non-stationarity could produce it, and no control rules these out.
concerns.quote: It would naturally produce β > 1 that grows as heat accumulates.

concerns.concern: The rising cycle-to-cycle correlation may come from cumulative heating and incomplete Off-state relaxation between rapid pulses, a thermal-memory effect rather than plastic learning.
concerns.quote: That is a thermal-memory effect, not plastic "learning."

concerns.concern: A sub-threshold, non-switching current shows the same β evolution as 4 mA, and 1.7 mA lies below the threshold. This undermines the claimed link between jamming and filament formation or switching determinism.
concerns.quote: the link between jamming and filament formation or switching determinism, which is central to the title, is undermined rather than supported.

concerns.concern: No cycle-resolved electrical data (switching voltage or time distributions, On-state resistance, variance before and after training) support the claim of deterministic switching.
concerns.quote: "Deterministic switching" is a statement about electrical behavior, yet no cycle-resolved electrical data are shown

concerns.concern: The jamming interpretation lacks independent signatures such as dynamic heterogeneity, ballistic τ ∝ 1/q scaling, yielding behavior or an order parameter.
concerns.quote: No independent signatures of jamming or glassiness are presented.

concerns.concern: The jamming time is measured under constant current while learning occurs under cycling, so the causal link between them asserted in the title is not established.
concerns.quote: t_jam is measured under constant current while learning occurs under cycling, so their causal link in the title is not yet established.

concerns.concern: Normalizing the correlation function by the whole-acquisition ⟨I²⟩ instead of standard pixel-averaged normalization makes any change in total intensity appear as decorrelation.
concerns.quote: With this normalization, any change in total diffracted intensity appears as "decorrelation" or as variations along the diagonal

concerns.concern: Off-state images are not recorded or analysed, so it is unknown whether the device returns to a distinct insulating configuration each cycle.
concerns.quote: Off-state images are not recorded or analysed to show whether the device returns to a distinct insulating configuration each cycle.

concerns.concern: There is no pulsed sub-threshold control with the same duty cycle to separate heating or drift from switching-induced reconfiguration.
concerns.quote: There is no pulsed sub-threshold control (same duty cycle, no filament) to separate heating/drift from switching-induced reconfiguration.

concerns.concern: Beam and sample drift (Bragg peak centroid, total intensity, sample position) is not monitored across the long runs.
concerns.quote: There is no beam/sample-drift monitoring (Bragg peak centroid, total intensity, sample position) across the 5,000 s run.

concerns.concern: No correlation matrix versus cycle lag is shown to demonstrate that late cycles converge to a common configuration rather than merely evolving slowly.
concerns.quote: There is no correlation matrix vs lag k (ΔG(n, n+k)) showing that late cycles converge to a common attractor rather than merely evolving slowly.

concerns.concern: Ga-irradiation defects, claimed to guide filament formation, could themselves explain deterministic switching. This is not disentangled from plasticity, and pristine-device results are only in the SI without quantitative comparison.
concerns.quote: The role of Ga-induced defects... could themselves explain deterministic switching, is not disentangled from the claimed plasticity.

concerns.concern: The proposed train/reset scheme (training, then sub-threshold erasure, then restored stochasticity) is never demonstrated in one protocol, and retention after training is not tested.
concerns.quote: The proposed train/reset scheme is never actually shown in one protocol

concerns.concern: Main-text results appear to come from single runs on single devices, with no repeats and no dependence on current amplitude or duty cycle.
concerns.quote: Each main-text result appears to come from a single run on a single device.

concerns.concern: Possible X-ray beam damage or beam-induced reduction from hours of focused exposure is not controlled for.
concerns.quote: Beam damage or beam-induced reduction is known for vanadium oxides.

concerns.concern: The beam is larger than the device and illuminates non-switching regions. Their static speckle causes heterodyne-like mixing that lowers contrast and can distort β.
concerns.quote: Non-switching regions contribute static speckle, producing heterodyne-like mixing. This lowers contrast and can distort β.

concerns.concern: The coherence length is much smaller than the device, and the filament's fraction of the scattering volume is not estimated. It is unclear whether XPCS probes the filament or the surrounding matrix.
concerns.quote: It is unclear whether XPCS is sensitive to the filament or mainly to the surrounding matrix.

concerns.concern: The 1 s exposure integrates over the whole On state and so does not probe the filament-nucleation event that determines stochasticity.
concerns.quote: The 1 s exposure also integrates over the entire On state, so it does not probe the filament-nucleation event that determines stochasticity.

concerns.concern: The shear-thickening analogy and the 'transition' claim rest on statistically indistinguishable jamming times, a missing plateau at 4 mA, and scattered β values with large errors.
concerns.quote: rests on t_jam = 1100 ± 600, 1200 ± 500, and 4000 ± 3000 s, which are statistically indistinguishable.

concerns.concern: The activation energy is derived from only two temperatures, one inside the non-stationary transition region, so it is not robust.
concerns.quote: An activation energy from two points with ~30% error is not robust.

concerns.concern: Comparing the activation energy to the melting temperature is not physically justified, because the two are not commensurate quantities.
concerns.quote: Activation barriers for domain-wall motion and the thermodynamic melting temperature are not commensurate quantities

concerns.concern: The local temperature under current is never estimated (e.g., from Bragg peak shift), although the interpretation relies heavily on Joule heating.
concerns.quote: The actual local temperature under 4 mA is never estimated (e.g., from Bragg peak shift)

concerns.concern: Mechanistic claims, such as metallic domains reducing available space or domains moving toward the filament, lack real-space or phase-fraction evidence, even though R/M1 intensities could test them.
concerns.quote: are offered without real-space or phase-fraction data, even though the R/M1 integrated intensities could at least test the first hypothesis.

concerns.concern: The ROI/pixels used, whether M1 and R peaks are captured simultaneously, and how speckle contrast A is determined are not specified.
concerns.quote: The authors do not specify which pixels or ROI are used, whether the M1 and R peaks are captured simultaneously, or how the speckle contrast A is determined.

concerns.concern: The normalization of the cycle-to-cycle correlation ΔG is undefined, and the text refers to a nonexistent inset.
concerns.quote: ΔG(n,n+1) is "normalized" to 0–1 without the normalization being defined.

concerns.concern: The main text says local irradiation of a central region, while Methods say global irradiation.
concerns.quote: The main text says a central 5×5 µm region was irradiated with 0.1 pC/µm²; Methods say devices were "globally irradiated."

concerns.concern: The domain-size estimate ignores finite-thickness and strain broadening.
concerns.quote: The domain size R_d = 2π/Q_FWHM ≈ 20 nm ignores finite-thickness (45 nm) and strain broadening.

concerns.concern: The paper does not discuss the gap between the ~10³ s timescales and practical neuromorphic operating speeds.
concerns.quote: Discuss the gap between the 10³-s timescales and practical neuromorphic operating speeds.

concerns.concern: There are multiple textual errors: 0.26 vs 0.27 mA, 150,000 vs 160,000 s, 'single exponential' for a stretched/compressed form, t₁ + t₂ = t_age, and Fig. 1 caption labels.
concerns.quote: Fix the textual errors

concerns.concern: Calling VO₂ a 'Mott insulator' is questionable given the debated Peierls/Mott character.
concerns.quote: "Mott insulator" terminology for VO₂, given the debated Peierls/Mott character.
